findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all custom grant-type factories
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an SPI implemented by out-of-tree/custom grant types. Adding getShortcut() as an abstract interface method means every existing custom factory no longer compiles and, if deployed as an old binary, throws AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() iterates provider factories. This is a breaking SPI change for a feature that could degrade gracefully. The method should be a default method (e.g. returning the unknown shortcut) so existing grants continue to work.

findings.title: Copy constructor of OAuth2GrantType.Context removed and constructor can now NPE
findings.body: The public Context(Context) copy constructor is deleted, breaking any grant implementation that cloned/modified the context before processing. In addition the remaining constructor now unconditionally calls formParams.getFirst(GRANT_TYPE), so code that constructed a Context with null formParams (previously valid) now throws NullPointerException at construction. Both changes break external grant types without a deprecation path.

findings.title: Token issuance now fails for unknown or unregistered grant types
findings.body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() copies the raw GRANT_TYPE attribute into AccessTokenContext, and encodeTokenId() throws IllegalStateException if that string has no registered shortcut. TokenManager.initToken() now calls this for every access token, so any flow or custom grant that sets a grant_type value that is not exactly a registered OAuth2GrantType factory id (or a custom provider returning a null/duplicate shortcut, which also causes a ConcurrentHashMap NPE in the factory refresh path) will fail token creation with a 500 instead of issuing a token. Previously such tokens were issued with a plain UUID. Encoding should fall back to the 'na' unknown shortcut rather than aborting issuance.

findings.title: Lightweight-token detection uses ambient context client and can NPE or misclassify
findings.body: getShouldUseLightweightToken(session) reads session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(...) (AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper line 86) and does not use the client from clientSessionContext. TokenManager.initToken() is invoked from flows where the KeycloakContext client is not set or differs from the client session's client (e.g. internally created/exchanged tokens), so this can throw NullPointerException during initToken or encode 'lt'/'rt' based on the wrong client. The client should be taken from clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getClient() and null-checked.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher is inverted and off-by-one
findings.body: The encoded prefix is 2 chars session type + 2 chars token type + 2 chars grant type, so the grant shortcut is substring(4,6), not substring(3,5). The matcher also returns false when substring equals expectedGrantShortcut and otherwise does not reject a mismatching grant at all. Consequently expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken will fail for correct tokens and pass for wrong grant types, masking regressions. It should be: if (!items[0].substring(4,6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false; (with a length guard to avoid StringIndexOutOfBounds).

findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: Line 73 calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...). A null rawTokenId therefore passes construction and produces a token id ending in ':null' from encodeTokenId(), instead of failing fast as the message intends.
